name: Muslim Advocates
mission: Working to promote justice and equity while protecting the diverse spectrum of Muslim communities from anti-Muslim discrimination in all of its forms.
theoryOfChange: Muslim Advocates outlines its strategic framework in its Annual Report. The organization details 'Our Strategies' which include high-impact legal advocacy, policy engagement, advocacy that builds community power, and narrative-shifting communications work. They measure their impact against three pillars: building community power, dismantling discriminatory systems, and demanding shared wellbeing. The report elaborates on how they measure success within these pillars, such as communities' ability to develop, organize, and act to influence decision-makers and create transformative change.

rich_narrative.summary: Muslim Advocates faces severe financial efficiency issues that limit its overall effectiveness. In FY2024, the organization generated <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $1,891,645</cite>. However, its program expense ratio stood at just <cite id="3">53.9%</cite>, leaving nearly half of its expenditures allocated toward administrative and fundraising overhead. This efficiency level falls well below the 75% sector benchmark and the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 79.4%</cite> for advocacy groups. A primary financial concern is executive compensation, as <cite id="1">CEO pay reached $222,356</cite>, representing roughly 11.8% of total revenue—a figure that triggers overhead scrutiny for an organization under $5 million in revenue. Additionally, fundraising efficiency is low, requiring <cite id="1">$0.53 to raise every $1</cite>. On a operational level, the group maintains a functional baseline, preserving <cite id="1">7.8 months of working capital</cite> to support ongoing litigation. It focuses on vital civil rights issues, providing <cite id="15">legal representation and policy engagement</cite> to defend American Muslims against discrimination. The charity maintains <cite id="2">zakat-eligible programming</cite> for its legal advocacy. Nevertheless, potential donors must weigh its specialized legal impact against high overhead costs and low spending efficiency.
